FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft linalized by the Automotive Primemovers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. The present day emphasis is on controlling of emissions from automobiles. For evaluating emissions of gaseous pollutants a standard was felt necessary and it resulted in the preparation of this Indian Standard. With the increasing emphasis on environment, the Government of India has already come out with legislation under Central Motor Vehicle Rules for the new vehicles fitted with spark ignition (petrol) engines to check and confirm that the gaseous pollutants in the exhaust of the vehicles are within the specified limits. While formulating ECE R-15 the standard considerable assistance has been derived from the following:

Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles equipped with a positive-ignition engine or with a compression-ignition engine with regard to the emiss.ion of gaseous pollutants by the engine - Method of measuring the power of positive-ignition engines -Method of measuring the fuel consumption of vehicles. Details of Standards for Emission of Gaseous Pollutants from Petrol Engine Vehicles and Test Procedures Effective from 01.04.1991. (Part III of Dot No. MOST/CMVR/TAP 115-l 16). of evaporative and crankcase emissions are separately covered by the following of crankcase

Annexure III of Ranganathan Committee Report The method of measurement Indian Standards: IS 13824 : 1993 IS 14555 : 1998

AUTOMOTIVE VEHICLES - EXHAUST EMISSIONS - GASEOUS POLLUTANTS FROM VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINES - METHOD OF MEASUREMENT
1 SCOPE This standard covers the method of test for the measurement/determination of gaseous pollutants from vehicles fitted with internal combustion engines and also the requirements of the equipment used for the tests. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 9057: 1998 Title Automotive vehicles - Exhaust emissions - Carbon monoxide concentration from vehicles equipped with spark ignition engines - Method of measurement Automotive vehicles - Gaseous pollutants from vehicles equipped with compression ignition engines - Method of measurement Automotive vehicles - Exhaust emissions - Equipment for the measurement of carbon monoxide concentration from vehicles equipped with spark ignition engines at idling - Specification Automotive vehicles - Performance requirements (measurement of power, SFC and opacity) of positive ignition and compression ignition engines - Method of test the case of vehicles with manual or semi-automatic transmission, or with selector in park or neutral position when an automatic transmission is installed, as recommended by the manufacturer. 3.2 Normal Thermal Conditions

Means the thermal conditions attained by an engine and its drive line after a run of at least 15 min on a variable course, under normal traffic conditions. 3.3 Gaseous Pollutants Means Carbon monoxide, Hydrocarbons (assuming a ratio of CHt.85) and oxides of Nitrogen (expressed in Nitrogen oxide NO equivalent). 3.4 Unladen Mass Means the mass of the vehicle in running order without crew, passengers or load, but with the fuel tank 90 percent full and the usual set of tools and spare wheel on board where applicab!e. In the case of 3-wheeled tractors, designed to be coupled to a semi-trailer, the unladen mass shall be that of the drawing vehicle. 3.5 Reference Mass Means the `Unladen Mass' of the vehicle increased by a uniform figure of 75 kg for 2-wheeled vehicles and 150 kg for all other vehicles. 3.6 Cold Start Device Means a device which enriches the air fuel mixture of the engine temporarily and thus assists engine to start and is similar to a choke. 3.1 Starting Aid Means a device which assists engine to start without enrichment of the fuel mixture such as glow plug, change of injection timing for fuel-injected spark ignition engine. 4 TEST REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The vehicle when subjected to Type I and Type II tests stipulated below shall meet the specified limits.

3 TERMINOLOGY

For the purpose of this standard in addition to the terms given in IS 14599 the following definitions shall apply. 3.1 Idle Speed

Means the engine speed, in revolution per minute, with fuel system controls (accelerator and choke) in the rest position, transmission in neutral and clutch engaged in 1

IS 14600 : 1999 4.2 Type I Test (Test for Verifying Emissions of Gaseous Pollutants) 4.2.1 Test Proeedl1r.e the Average 4.2.2 4.2.2.1 Operuting Cycle 0~ the Chassis Dynamometer Description of the cycle

4.2.1.1 The vehicle shall be placed on adynamometer bench equipped with a means of load and inertia simulation. A test lasting a total duration of 648 s and comprising six cycles as stipulated in 4.2.2 shall be carried out, without interruption. During the test, the exhaust gases shall be diluted with air and a proportional sample collected in one or more bags. The contents of the bags shall be analysed at the end of the test. The total volume of the diluted exhaust shall be measured. The methods used to collect and analyse the gases shall be those specified. Other analysis methods may be approved if it is found that they yield equivalent results. The test shall be repeated three times. In case test is carried out for verification of compliance to statutory limits the condition stipulated in 4.2.1.4 shall apply. 4.2.X2 For each of the pollutants, not more than one of the three results obtained may exceed by not more than 10 percent of the limit specified for that type of vehicle, provided the arithmetical mean of the three results rounded off to the second decimal place is not exceeding the specified limit. Where the specified limits are exceeded for more than one pollutant, it shall be immaterial whether this occurs in the same test or in different tests. 4.2.1.3 If one of the three results obtained of each of the pollutants exceeds by more than 10 percent the limit prescribed for that type of vehicle specified, the test may be continued as specified below. The number of tests specified in 4.2.1.1 may be increased to ten provided that the arithmetical mean 0 of the three results falls between 100 and 110 percent of the limit (L). In this case, the decision, after testing, shall depend exclusively on the average results obtained from all 10 tests (rounded off to the second decimal place), with respect to the limits. 4.2.1.4 The number of tests specified in 4.2.1.1 shall be reduced in the conditions hereinafter specified, where VI is the result of the first test and V2 the result of the second test for each of the pollutants. Only one test shall be carried out if VI readings of any of the pollutants is less than or equal to 0.70 L (VI IO.70 L). Only two tests shall be carried out if the levels of the pollutants are VI I 0.85 L, and if, at the same time, one of these values is VI > 0.70 L. In addition, the Vz readings of the pollutants shall satisfy the requirement that (VI + V;! ) I 1.70 L and V2 I L. 4.2.1.5 The flow chart for the type approval tests is shown in Fig. 1.

The operating cycle on the chassis dynamometer shall be as notified by the statutory authorities. The details of IDC are indicated in Tables 1 and 2 and shown in Fig. 2. In case the testing is carried out for any other driving cycle the details shall be given in the test report. Preliminary testing cycles should be carried out if necessary to determine how best to actuate the accelerator and brake controls so as to achieve a cycle approximately to the theoretical cycle within the specified limits. IS 14600 : 1999 4.2.2.3 Manual change gear-box in Annex A. It shall also be run-in as recommended the manufacturer. by

During each phase at constant speed, the rotating speed of the engine shall be, if possible, between 50 and 90 percent of the speed corresponding to the maximum power of the engine. When this speed can be reached in two or more gears, the vehicle shall be tested with the higher gear engaged. During acceleration, the vehicle shall be tested in whichever gear is appropriate to the acceleration imposed by the cycle. A higher gear shall be engaged at the latest when the rotating speed is equal to 110 percent of the speed corresponding to the maximum power of the engine. During deceleration, a lower gear shall be engaged before the engine starts to idle roughly, at the latest when the engine revolutions are equal to 30 percent of the speed corresponding to the maximum power of the engine. No change down to first gear shall be effected during deceleration. Vehicles equipped with an overdrive which the driver can actuate shall be tested with the overdrive disengaged. 4.2.2.4 When it is not possible to adhere to the cycle, the operating cycle shall be modified for gear change points, allowing two seconds time interval at constant speed for each gear change keeping the total time constant. The operating cycle with recommended gear positions is shown in Fig. 3. 4.2.2.5 Automatic gear-box

4.2.4.2 The exhaust device shall not exhibit any leak likely to reduce the quantity of gas collected and this shall be the same emerging from the engine. 4.2.4.3 It shall also be ensured system is leak proof. that the air intake

4.2.4.4 The settings of the engine and of the vehicle's controls shall be those recommended by the manufacturer. This requirement also applies, in particular, to the settings for idling and for the cold start device, automatic choke and exhaust gas cleaning systems, etc. 4.2.4.5 The vehicle to be tested, or an equivalent vehicle, shall be fitted, if necessary with a device to permit the measurement of characteristic parameters necessary for the chassis dynamometer setting. 4.2.4.6 The testing agency may verify that the vehicle conforms to the performance of power, acceleration, maximum speed, etc, stated by the manufacturer and that it can be used for normal driving and more particularly that it is capable of starting both in hot and cold conditions. 4.2.4.7 The test vehicle should be run-in as per the manufacturer's specifications before the test. 4.2.5 Fuel The requirements of reference fuel shall be the same as notified by the statutory authorities. A commercially available fuel may also be used provided that the characteristics are such that it does not contain any smoke supressant additives. 4.2.6 4.2.6.1 a) Test Equipment Chassis dynamometer The dynamometer shall be capable of simulating road load and any one of the following classifications: 9 Dynamometer with fixed load curve, that is a dynamometer whose physical characteristics provide a fixed load curve is not a preferred type of dynamometer. ii) Dynamometer with adjustable load curve that is a dynamometer with at least two road load parameters that can be adjusted to shape the load curve. This is a preferred type of dynamometer. The chassis dynamometer may have one or two rollers. In the case of a single roller, the roller diameter shall not be less than 400 mm for 2-wheelers and 1 200 mm for other vehicles.

Vehicles equipped with automatic shift gear-boxes shall be tested with the highest gear (drive) engaged. The accelerator shall be used in such a way as to obtain the steadiest acceleration possible, enabling the various gears to be engaged in the normal order. 4.2.3 Tolerances

4.2.3.1 A tolerance of +l km/h shall be allowed between the indicated speed and the theoretical speed during acceleration, during steady speed and during deceleration, when the vehicle's brakes are used. If the vehicle decelerates more rapidly without the use of the brakes, then the timing of the theoretical cycle shall be restored by constant speed or idling period merging into the following operation. Speed tolerances greater than those recommended shall be accepted, during phase changes provided that the tolerances never exceed 0.5 s on any one occasion. 4.2.3.2 Time tolerances of + 0.5 s shall be allowed. The above tolerances shall apply equally at the beginning and at the end of each gear changing period. 4.2.3.3 The speed and time combined as shown in Fig. 2. 4.2.4 Test Vehicle tolerances shall be

IS 14600 : 1999 c) The setting of the dynamometer shall not be affected by the lapse of time. It shall not produce any vibrations perceptible to the vehicle and likely to impair the vehicle's normal operations. It shall be equipped with means to simulate inertia and load. These simulators shall be connected to the front roller, in the case of a two roller dynamometer. The roller shall be fitted with a revolution counter with reset facility to measure the distance actually travelled. Accuracy i) It shall be possible to record the indicated load to an accuracy of + 5 percent. ii) In case of dynamometer with a fixed load curve the accuracy of the load setting at 40 km/h shall be f 5 percent. In case of a dynamometer with adjustable load curve, the accuracy of matching dynamometer load to road load shall be within f 5 percent at 30,40 and 50 km/h and + 10 percent at 20 km/h. Below this, the dynamometer absorption shall be positive. iii) The total equivalent inertia of the rotating parts (including the simulated inertia where applicable) shall be known and within + 20 kg of the inertia class for the test, in case of four-wheeled vehicles; for two-wheeled vehicles within f 2 percent. iv) The speed of the vehicle shall be measured by the speed of rotation of the roller (the front roller in the case of a two roller dynamometer). It shall be measured with an accuracy of f 1 km/h at speeds above 10 km/h. Load and inertia setting i) Dynamometer with adjustable load curve: the load simulator shall be adjusted in order to absorb the power exerted on the driving wheels at various steady speeds. ii) Chassis dynamometer with fixed load curve: the load simulator shall be adjusted to absorb the power exerted on the driving wheels at a steady speed of 40 km/h. iii) The means by which these loads are determined and set are stipulated in Annex B. Inertia dynamometers with electrical inertia simulation shall be demonstrated to be equivalent to mechanical inertia systems. The means by which equivalence is established is stipulated in Annex C. 7 h) Chassis dynamometer calibration i) The dynamometer shall be calibrated at least once in a month or performance verified at least once in a week and then calibrated as required. The shall consist of the calibration manufacturers' recommended procedure and a determination of the dynamometer frictional power absorption at 40 km/h. A method for determining this is given in Annex D. Other methods may be used if they are proven to yield equivalent results. ii) The performance check consists of conducting dynamometer coast down time at one or more inertia power setting and comparing the coast down time to that recorded during the last calibration. If the coast down time differs by more than a new calibration is one second, required. Exhaust gas sampling system The exhaust gas sampling system shall be designed to enable the measurement of the true A Conmass emissions of vehicle exhaust. stant Volume Sampler System wherein the vehicle exhaust is continuously diluted with ambient air under controlled conditions shall be used. In the constant volume sampler concept of measuring mass emissions, two conditions shall be satisfied, the total volume of the mixture of exhaust and dilution air shall be measured and a continuously proportional sample of the volume shall be collected for analysis. Mass emissions are determined from the sample concentrations, corrected for the pollutant content of the ambient air and totalized flow, over the test period. The flow through the system shall be sufficient to eliminate water condensation at all conditions which may occur during a test, as outlined in Annex E. A schematic diagram of the general concept is shown in Fig. 4. Examples of three types of Constant Volume Sampler Systems which shall meet the requirements are outlined in Annex E. The gas and air mixture shall be homogeneous at point S2 of the sampling probe (see Fig. 4). The probe shall extract a true sample of the diluted exhaust gases. The system shall be free from gas leaks. The design and materials shall be such that the system does not influence the pollutant concentration in the diluted exhaust gas. IS 14600 : 1999 likely to change the concentration of any pollutant gas in the diluted gas, then the sampling for that pollutant shall be carried out before that component, if the problem cannot be corrected. If the vehicle being tested is equipped with an exhaust pipe comprising several branches, all of them shall be connected as near as possible to the vehicle. Static pressure variations at the tailpipe(s) of the vehicle shall remain within f 1.25 kPa of the static pressure variations measured during the dynamometer driving cycle and with no connection to the tailpipe(s). Sampling systems capable of maintaining the static pressure to within f 0.25 kPa shall be used if a written request from a manufacturer to the testing agency granting the approval substantiates the need for the closer tolerance. The back-pressure shall be measured in the exhaust pipe as near as possible to its end or in an extension having the same diameter. The various valves used to direct the exhaust gases shall be of a quick-adjustment, quickacting type. The gas samples shall be collected in sample bags of adequate capacity. These bags shall be made of such materials that do not change the pollutant gas by more than f 2 percent after 20 min of storage. Analytical equipment Pollutant gases shall be analysed with the ,following instruments i) &bon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (C02) analysis The carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide analysers shall be of the NonDispersive Infra Red (NDIR) absorption ii) type. Hydrocarbon (HC) analysis (Gasoline vehicles) The hydrocarbon analyser shall be of the Flame Ionization (FID) type calibrated with propane gas expressed equivalent to carbon atoms. Hydrocarbons (HC) analysis (Diesel vehicles) The hydrocarbon analyser shall be of the Flame Ionization type with Detector, pipe work, etc, heated to. Valves, 463 + 10 K (HFID). It shall be calibrated with propane gas expressed equivalent to carbon atoms (Cl ). Nitrogen oxide (NOx) analysis The nitrogen oxide analyser chall be of the Chemiluminescent (CLA) type with an NOx-NO converter. 9

b) Accuracy
The analysers shall have a measuring range compatible with the accuracy required to measure the concentrations of the exhaust gas sample pollutants. Measurement errors shall not exceed + 3 percent disregarding the true value of the calibration gases. For concentrations of less than 100 ppm the measurement error shall not exceed f 3 ppm. The ambient air sample shall be measured on the same analyser and range as the corresponding diluted exhaust sample. c) Ice-trap No gas drying device shall be used before the analysis unless it is known that it has no effect on the pollutant content of the gas stream. 4 Particular requirements for compression ignition engines A heated sample line for a continuous HCanalysis with the flame ionization detector (HFID), including recorder (R) shall be used. The average concentration of the measured hydrocarbons shall be determined by integration. Throughout the test, the temperature of the heated sample line shall be controlled at 463 f 10 K. The heated sampling line shall be fitted with a heated filter (6;~) (99 percent efficient with particle size < 0.3 pm) to extract any solid particles from the continuous flow of gas required for analysis. The sampling system response time (from the probe to the analyser inlet) shall not exceed 4 s. The HFID shall be used with a constant flow (heat exchanger) system to ensure a representative sample, unless compensation for varying CFV or CFO flow is made. Calibration Each analyser shall be calibrated as often as necessary and in any case in the month before type approval testing and at least once every six months for verifying conformity of production. The calibration method that shall be used is outlined in D-4 for the analysers indicated in 4.2. Volume measurement The method of measuring total dilute exhaust volume incorporated in the constant volume sampler shall be such that measurement is accurate to within + 2 percent. Constant volume sampler calibration The Constant Volume Sampler System volume measurement device shall be calibrated by a suitable method to ensure the specified accuracy and at a frequency sufficient to maintain such accuracy.

4.2.6.6 The exhaust gas-sampling system shall be verified by the method given in D-5. The maximum 10

4.2.7.3 Four-wheel drive vehicles shall be tested in a two-wheel drive mode of operation. Permanent four-wheel drive vehicles shall have one set of drive wheels temporarily disengaged by the vehicle

IS 14600 : 1999 manufacturers. Four-wheel drive vehicles which can be manually shifted to a two-wheel drive mode shall be tested in the normal mode on-highway two-wheel drive mode of operation. 4.2.8 Procedure for Chassis Dynamometer 4.2.8.1 a) Test 30 and 45 cm in front of its front wheel. The device used to measure the linear velocity of the air shall be located in the middle of the stream at 20 cm away from the air outlet. The air velocity shall be 25 + 5 km/h. This velocity shall be as nearly constant as possible across the whole of the blower outlet surface. During the test, the speed shall be recorded with respect to time so that the correctness of the cycles performed can be assured. Starting of the engine The engine shall be started by means of the devices provided for this purpose according to the manufacturer's recommendations, as incorporated in the driver's handbook of production vehicles. Warming up of the vehicle shall be done on the chassis dynamometer as per manufacturer's recommendations by using the operating test cycles. The test cycle shall begin at the end of this warming up period. If the maximum speed of the vehicle is less than the maximum speed of the driving cycle, that part of the driving cycle, where speed is exceeding the vehicle's maximum speed, the vehicle shall be driven with fully open the throttle. Idling Manual-shif or semi-automatic gear-box i) During periods of idling, the clutch shall be engaged and gears shall be in neutral position. ii) To enable the accelerations to be performed according to normal cycle the vehicle shall be pla$ed in first gear, with clutch disengaged, 5 s before the acceleration following the idling period considered. iii) The first idling period at the beginning of the cycle shall consist of 11 s of idling in neutral with the clutch engaged and 5 s in first gear with the clutch disengaged. Automatic-shifr gear-box After initial engagement, the selector shall not be operated at any time during the test except in accordance with 4.2.8.4 (b).

Special conditions for carrying out the cycle During the test, the cell temperature shall be between 298 K and 313 K. The absolute humidity (H) of either the air in the test cell or the intake air of the engine shall be such that 5.55 HI18gHzO/kgdryair. The vehicle shall be approximately horizontal during the test to avoid any abnormal distribution of the fuel. The tyre pressure shall be the same as that recommended by the manufacturer and used for the preliminary road test for data collection for adjustment of chassis dynamometer. The tyre pressure may be increased up to 50 percent from the manufacturer's recommended setting in the case of a two roll dynamometer in order to prevent tyre damage. The actual pressure used shall be recorded in the test report. Cooling of the vehicle i) For vehicles with liquid cooled engines the test shall be carried out with the bonnet raised unless this is technically impossible. An auxiliary ventilating device acting on the radiator (water cooling) or on the air intake (air cooling) may be used if necessary, to keep the engine temperature normal. ii) For vehicles with air cooled engines throughout the test, an auxiliary cooling blower shall be positioned in front of the vehicle, so as to direct cooling air to the engine. The blower speed shall be such that, within the operating range of 10 to 50 km/h the linear velocity of the air at the blower outlet is within + 5 km/h of the corresponding roller speed. At roller speeds of less than 10 km/h, air velocity may be zero, the blower outlet shall have a cross section area of at least 0.4 m2 and the bottom of the blower outlet shall be between 15 and 20 cm above floor level. The blower outlet shall be perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle between 30 and 45 cm in front of its front wheel. iii) As an alternative, an auxiliary cooling blower may be positioned in front of the vehicle. The blower outlet shall have a cross sectional area of at least 0.4 m2 and shall be perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle between

4.2.8.4 Accelerations a) Manual-shift gear-box i> Accelerations shall be so performed that the rate of acceleration is as constant as possible through the phase.

11

IS 14600 :1999 ii) If an acceleration cannot be carried out in the specified time, the extra time required shall be deducted from the time allowed for changing the combination, if possible, and'in any case, from the subsequent steady-speed or deceleration period.

4

b) Automatic-shift gear-boxes If an acceleration cannot be carried out in the specified time the gear selector shall be operated in accordance with requirements for manual-shift gear-boxes. 4.2.8.5 Decelerations All decelerations shall be effected by closing the throttle completely. The clutch shall be disengaged, at around a speed of 10 km/h. b) If rhe period of deceleration is longer than that specified for the corresponding phase, the vehicle's brakes shall be used to enable the timing of the cycle to be abided by. c) If the period of deceleration is shorter than that specified for the corresponding phase, the timing of theoretical cycle shall be restored by constant speed or idling period merging into the following operation. 4 At the end of the deceleration period (halt of the vehicle on the rollers) the gears shall be placed in neutral and the clutch engaged.
4.2.8.6Steady speeds

The analysers' zeros shall then be re-checked. If the reading differs by more than 2 percent of range from that set in (b), the procedure shall be repeated. The samples shall then be analysed. After the analysis zero and span points shall be re-checked using the same gases. If these rechecks are within 2 percent of those in (b) above then the analysis shall be considered acceptable. 8) For all the points in this section, the flow rates and pressure of the various gases shall be the same as those used during calibration of the analysers. h) The value of the content of the gases in each of the pollutants measured shall be that recorded after stabilization of the measuring device. Diesel hydrocarbon mass emissions shall be calculated from the integrated HFID reading corrected for varying flow, if necessary, as shown in Annex D.
of the Quantity of Gaseous

4.2.10 Determination

Pollutants Emitted 4.2.10.1 The volume considered

The volume to be considered shall be corrected to

conform to the conditions of 101.3 kPa and 293 K. 4.2.10.2 Total mass of gaseous pollutants emitted The mass, M, of each pollutant emitted by the vehicle during the test shall be determined by obtaining the product of the voluminal concentration and the volume of the gas in question, with due regard for the following densities at the above mentioned reference condition. In the case of carbon monoxide (CO) d = 1.164 kg/m3. In the case of hydrocarbons (CH1.85) d = 0.576 8 kg/m3. In the case of nitrogen oxides (NOz)d = 1.913 kg/m3. 4.2.10.3 Annex F describes the calculations for the various methods to determine the qtiantity of gaseous pollutants emitted. 4.3 Type II Test (Test for Carbon Monoxide Emissions at Idling Speed) This test is applicable only for vehicles fitted with spark ignition engines. This test shall be carried out as per IS 9057 immediately after the sixth operating cycle of the Type I test, with the engine at idling speed, the cold start device not being used . For facilitating measurement with CVS system the sampling probe can be placed in the pipe connecting the exhaust with CVS system and as close to the exhaust pipe as possible. On manufacturers request, a retest shall be carried out, with the sampling probe mounted as per IS 9057.

a)

b)

`Pumping' or the closing of the throttle shall be avoided when passing from acceleration to the following steady speed. Periods of constant speed shall be achieved by keeping the accelerator in fixed position.

4.2.9 Procedure for Sampling and Analysis
4.2.9.1 Sampling

Sampling shall start at the beginning of the test cycle as given in 4.2.8.2 (b) and at the end of the sixth cycle. 4.2.9.2 Analysis a) The exhaust gases contained in the bag shall be analysed at the earliest but not later than 20 min after the end of the test cycle. b) Prior to each sample analysis the analyser range to be used for each pollutant shall be set to zero with the appropriate zero gas. c) The analysers shall then be set to the calibration curves by means of span gases of nominal concentrations of 70 to 100 percent of the range.

B-6.3 Additional Setting Methods of Setting for Two-Wheeled Vehicles B-6.3.1 The brake shall be so adjusted as to reproduce the operation of the vehicle on the level road at a steady speed between 35 and 45 km/h (or maximum speed in case of mopeds). B-6.3.2 Road Test B-6.3.2.1 Accuracies of test equipment Time shall be measured accurate to within 0.1 s and speed shall be measured accurate to within 2 percent. B-6.3.2.2 An adjustable stop, limiting the maximum speed to between 35 km/h and 45 km/h shall be mounted in the fuel-feed regulating device. The speed of the vehicle shall be measured by means of precision speedometer or computed from the time measured over a given distance on a level dry road in both directions, with the stop applied. B-6.3.2.3 The measurements, which shall be repeated at least three times in both directions shall be taken over a distance of at least 200 m and with a sufficiently long acceleration distance. The average speed shall be determined. E-6.3.2.4 In case of two-wheeled vehicles with maximum speed around 40 km/h, the maximum attainable speed on the road with throttle fully opened 24

B-6.2.2 Test Instrumentation

The vacuum (or absolute pressure) in the intake manifold of the vehicle shall be measured to an accuracy of f0.25 kPa. It shall be possible to record continuously this reading or at intervals of not more than one second. The speed shall be recorded continuously with a precision of kO.4 km/h. B-6.2.3 Koad Test

Drive the vehicle at a steady speed of 40 km/h recording speed and vacuum (or absolute pressure) within the requirement of B-5.2.2. B-6.2.4 Repeat procedure of B-5.2.2 three times in each direction. All six runs shall be completed within four hours. B-6.2.5 Data Reduction and Acceptance Criteria

B-6.2.5.1 Review results obtained in accordance with B-6.2.3 and B-6.2.4 (speed shall not be lower than 39.5 km/h or greater than 40.5 km/h for more than one second). For each run, read vacuum level at an interval of one second, calculate mean vacuum (v) and standard deviation(s). This calculation shall consist of not less than 10 readings of vacuum. B-6.2.5.2 The standard deviation shall not exceed 10 percent of mean (v! for each run. B-6.2.5.3 Calculate the mean value(v) for the six runs (three runs in each direction). D-2.1 The power absorbed by chassis dynamometer comprises the power absorbed by frictional effects and the power absorbed by the power absorption device. The chassis dynamometer is brought into operation beyond the range of test speeds. The device used for starting up the chassis dynamometer is then disconnected and the rotational speed of the driven rollers decreases. The kinetic energy of rollers is dissipated by the power absorption unit and by the frictional effects. This method disregards variations in the roller's internal frictional effects caused by rollers with or without the vehicle. The frictional effects of the rear roller shall be disregarded when this is free. D-2.2 Calibrating the Power Indicator to 40 km/h as a Function of the Power Absorbed The procedure outlined below shall be followed: D-2.2.1 Measure the rotational speed of the roller, if this has not already been done. A fifth wheel, a revolution counter or some other method may be used. D-2.2.2 Place the vehicle on the dynamometer or connect the device for starting up the dynamometer. D-2.2.3 Use the fly-wheel or any other system of inertia simulation for the particular inertia class to be used. D-2.2.4 Bring 40 km/h. D-2.2.5 the dynamometer to a speed of

IS 14600 : 1999 D-3.1.1 Various types of flow meters such as calibrated venturi, laminar flow meter, calibrated turbine meter may be used provided that they are dynamic measurement systems and can meet the requirements stipulated in 4.2.6.2 (b) and (c). D-3.1.2 The following sections give details of methods of calibration of PDP and CFV units, using a laminar flow meter, which gives the required accuracy together with a statistical check on the calibration validity. D-3.2 Calibration Pump (PUP) of the Positive Displacement D-3.2.3.1 The possible test SFt-up is shown in Fig. 6. Variations are permissible, provided that they are approved by the Authority granting the approval as being of comparable accuracy. If the set-up shown in Fig. 7 is used, the following data shall be found within the limits of precision given below: Barometric pressure (corrected) (PB)+ 0.03 kPa Ambient temperature (T) IL0.2 K Air temperature at LFE (ETI) f0.15 K Pressure depression upstream of LFE(EPI) f 0.01 kPa Pressure drop across the LFE matrix (EDP) f 0.0015 kPa Air temperature at CVS-pump inlet (PTI) f 0.2 K Air temperature at CVS-pump outlet (PTO) f 0.2 K Pressure depression at CVS-pump inlet (PPI) f 0.22 kPa Pressure head at CVS-pump outlet (PPO) rt 0.22 kPa Pump revolutions during test period (n) i 1 rev Elapsed time for period (Miiz 250 s) (t) kO.1 s D-3.2.3.2 After the system has been connected, as shown in Fig. 8, the variable restrictor is set in the wide-open position and the CVS-pump run for 20 min before starting the calibration. D-3.2.3.3 The restrictor valve is adjusted in steps to get an increment of pump inlet depression (about 1 kPa) that shall yields a minimum of six data points for the total calibration. The system shall be allowed to stabilize for three minutes and the data acquisition shall be repeated. D-3.2.4 Data Analysis

D-3.2.1 The following calibration procedure outlines the equipment, test configuration and the various parameters which shall be measured to establish the flow rate of the CVS-pump. All the parameters related to the pump shall be measured simultaneously with the parameters related to the flow meter which is connected in series with pump. The calculated flow rate (given in m3 /min) at pump inlet, absolute pressure and temperature can then be plotted versus a correlation function which is the value of a specific combination of pump parameters. The linear equation which relates the pump and the correlation function shall then be determined. In the event that a CVS has a multiple speed drive, a calibration for each range used shall be performed. D-3.2.2 This calibration procedure is based on the measurement of the absolute values of the pump and flow meter parameters that relate the flow rate at each point. The three conditions that are required to be maintained to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the calibration curve are outlined below. D-3.2.2.1 The pump pressures shall be measured at tappings on the pump rather than at the external piping on the pump inlet and outlet. Pressure taps that are mounted at the top centre and bottom centre of the pump drive headplate are exposed to the actual pump cavity pressures and therefore reflect the absolute pressure differentials. D-3.2.2.2 Temperature stability shall be maintained during the calibration. The laminar flow meter is sensitive to inlet temperature oscillations which cause the data points to be scattered. Gradual changes of f 1K in temperature are acceptable as long as they occur over a period of several minutes. D-3.2.2.3 All connections between the flow meter and the CVS-pump shall be free from any leakage. D-3.2.3 During an exhaust emission test, the measurement of these same pump parameters enables the user to calculate the flow rate from the calibration equation.

D-3.2.4.1 The air flow rate (Qs) at each test point shall be calculated in m3 /min from the flow meter data using the manufacturer's recommended method. D-3.2.4.2 The air flow rate is then converted to pump flow (V,) in rev/min at absolute pump inlet temperature and pressure. v,=,x293x where V, = pump flow rate at T, and P, m3 /rev, given in

D-4.3.1 A minimum of two hours shall be allowed for warming up of the infra-red NDIR analyser, but it is preferable that power be left on continuously in the analysers. The chopper motors may be turned off when not in use. D-4.3.2 Prior to each analysis each normally operating range shall be verified. used

D-4.3.3 Using purified dry air ( or Nitrogen ), the CO and NOx analysers shall be set at zero and dry air shall be purified for the HC analyser. D-4.3.4 Span gas having a concentration of the constituent that gives a 75-95 percent full-scale deflection shall be introduced and the gain set to match the calibration curve. The same flow rate shall be used for calibration, span and exhaust sampling to avoid correction for sample cell pressure. D-4.3.5 The nominal value of the span calibration gas used shall remain within + 2 percent of the calibration curve. D-4.3.6 If it does not, but it remains within f 5 percent of the calibration curve, the system parameters such as gain of the amplifier, turning of NDIR analysers, optimisation of FID analysers may be adjusted to bring within rt 2 percent. D-4.3.7 If the system does not meet the requirement of D-4.3.5 and D-4.3.6, the system shall be verified for any fault and shall be corrected and a new calibration curve shall be obtained. D-4.3.8 If required, zero shall be checked and the procedures specified in D-4.3.3 and D-4.3.4 shall be repeated. D-4.4 System Leak Test A system leakage test shall be performed. The probe shall be disconnected from the exhaust system and the end plugged. The analyser pump shall be switched on. After an initial stabilisation period all flow meters and pressure gauges shall read zero. If not, the

D-4.2.1 The calibration procedure shall be carried out as often as necessary and in any case within one month preceding the type approval emission test and once in six months for verifying conformity of production (COP). D-4.2.2 The verification shall be carried out using standard gases. The same gas flow rates shall be used as when sampling exhaust gas. D-4.2.3 A minimum of two hours shall be allowed for warming up of the analysers. D-4.2.4 The NDIR analyser shall be tuned, where appropriate and the flame combustion of the FID analyser shall be optimised. D-4.5.1 The efficiency of the convertor used for the convex-sion of NO2 into NO is obtained as follows. D-4.5.1.1 Using the test set up shown in Fig. 9 and the procedure specified below, the efficiency of the convertors can be obtained by means of an ozonator. D-4.5.2 Calibrate the CLA analyser in the most common operating range following the manufacturer's specification using zero and span gas (the NO content of which may amount to about 80 percent of the operating range and the NO2 concentration of the gas mixture shall be less than 5 percent of the NO concentration). The NOx analyser shall be in the NO mode so that span gas does not pass through the convertor. Record the indicated concentration. D-4.5.3 Oxygen or synthetic air is added continuously via a T-fitting to the gas flow until the concentration indicated is about 10 percent less than the indicated calibration concentration given in D-3.1. Record the indicated concentration (c). The ozonator shall be kept deactivated throughout this process. D-4.5.4 The ozonator is now activated to generate enough ozone to bring the NO concentration down to 20 percent (minimum 10 percent) of the calibration concentration given under D-4.1.2. Record the indicated concentration (4. D-4.5.5 The NOx analyser is then switched to the NOx mode which means that the gas mixture (consisting of NO, N02, 02 and N2) now passes through the convertor. Record the indicated concentration (u). The ozonator is now deactivated. D-4.5.6 The mixture of gases specified in D-4.5.3 passes through the convertor into the detector. Record the indicated concentration (b). D-4.5.7 With the ozonator deactivated, the flow of oxygen or synthetic air is also shut off. The NOx reading of the analyser shall then be no more than 5 percent above the value obtained as per D-4.5.2.

D-4.5.10 The efficiency of the convertor tested at least once a week. D-5 TOTAL SYSTEM VERIFICATION

D-5.1 In order to comply with the requirements of 4.2.4.6, total accuracy of the CVS, sampling and analytical systems shall be determined by introducing a known mass of a pollutant gas into the system while it is being operated as if during a normal test and then analysing and calculating the pollutant mass according to the formulae given in Annex E except that the density of propane shall be taken as 1.833 kg/m3 at standard conditions. The following two techniques are known to give sufficient accuracy. D-5.2 Metering a constant flow of pure gas (CO or C3Hg), using a critical flow orifice device, is fed into the CVS system through the calibrated critical orifice. If the inlet pressure is high enough, the flow rate 4, which is adjusted by means of the critical flow orifice is independent of orifice outlet pressure (critical flow). If deviations exceed by 5 percent, the cause of the malfunction shall be located and determined. Then CVS system operated as in an exhaust emission test for about 5 to 10 min. The gas collected in the sampling bag is analysed by the usual equipment and the results compared to known quantity of pure gas. D-5.3 Metering a limited quantity of pure gas (CO or C3Hg) by means of a gravimetric technique. The following gravimetric procedure may be used to verify the CVS system. The mass of a small cylinder filled with either carbon monoxide or propane is determined with a precision of +O.Ol g. The CVS system shall be operated for about 5 to 10 min as in a normal exhaust emission test, while CO or propane is injected into the system. The quantity of pure gas involved is determined by means of differential weighing. The gas accumulated in the bag is then analysed by means of the equipment normally used for the exhaust gas analysis. The results are then compared to the concentration values computed earlier.

GAS SAMPLING E-l SCOPE SYSTEMS E-2.1.3.4 A temperature control system (TC), used to preheat the heat exchanger before the test and to control its temperature during the test, so that deviations from the designed operating temperature are limited to + 6 K. E-2.1.3.5 The positive displacement pump (PDP), used to transport a constant volume flow of the air exhaust gas mixture. The flow capacity of the pump shall be large enough to eliminate water condensation in the system under all operating conditions which may occur during a test, this can be generally ensured by using a positive displacement pump with an adequate flow capacity twice as high as the maximum flow of exhaust gas produced by accelerations of the driving cycle or sufficient to ensure that the CO2 concentration in the dilute exhaust sample bag is less than 3 percent by volume. E-2.1.3.6 A temperature sensor (Tt) (accuracy and precision +l"C) fitted at a point immediately upstream of the positive displacement pump. It shall be designed to monitor continuously the temperature of diluted exhaust gas mixture during the test. E-2.1.3.7 A pressure gauge (Cl) (accuracy and precision + 0.4 kPa) fitted immediately upstream of the volume meter and used to register the pressure gradient between the gas mixture and the ambient air. E-2.1.3.8 Another pressure gauge (G2) (accuracy and precision +0.4 kPa) fitted so that the differential pressure between pump inlet and pump outlet can be registered. E-2.1.3.9 Two sampling outlets (St and S2) for taking constant samples of the dilution air and of the diluted exhaust gas/air mixture. E-2.1.3.10 A filter(F), to extract solid particles from the flow of gas collected for analysis. E-2.1.3.11 Pumps (P), to collect a constant flow of the dilution of air as well as of the diluted exhaust gas/air mixture during the test. E-2.1.3.12 Flow controllers (N), to ensure a constant uniform flow of the gas samples taken during the course of the test from sampling probes St and S2 and flow of the gas samples shall be such that, at the end of each test, the quantity of the samples is sufficient for analysis (about 10 Urnin.) E-2.1.3.13 monitoring test. Flow meters (FL), for adjusting and the constant flow of gas samples during the

E-3.1 This Annex describes two types of gas sampling systems meeting the requirements specified in 4.2.6.2. Another type specified in E-2.3, may be used if it complies these requirements. E-l.2 The laboratory shall record in its report the system of sampling used when performing the test. Systems not specified in this Annex could be used, if it is proven to give equivalent results. E-2 DESCRIPTION OF DEVICES Device with Positive

E-2.1 Variable Dilution Displacement Pump

E-2.1.1 The Positive Displacement Pump - Constant Volume Sampler (PDP-CVS) satisfies the requirements by metering at a constant temperature and pressure through the pump. The total volume is measured by counting the revolutions made by the calibrated positive displacement pump. The proportional sample is achieved by sampling with pump, flow meter and flow control valve at a constant flow rate. E-2.1.2 A schematic drawing of such a sampling system is shown in Fig. 10. Since various configurations can produce accurate results, exact conformity with the drawings is not essential. Additional components such as instruments, valves, solenoids and switches may be used to provide additional information and co-ordinate the functions of the component system. E-2.1.3 The collecting equipment shall consist of.

E-2.1.3.1 A filter (n) for the dilution air, which can be preheated, if necessary. This filter shall consist of activated charcoal sandwiched between two layers of paper and shall be used to reduce and stabilise the hydrocarbon concentrations of ambient emissions in the dilution air. E-2.1.3.2 A mixing chamber (M) in which exhaust gas and air are mixed homogeneously. E-2.1.3.3 A heat exchanger (H) of a capacity sufficient to ensure that throughout the test the temperature of the air/exhaust gas mixture measured at a point immediately upstream of the positive displacement pump is within f 6 K of the designed operating temperature. This device shall not affect the pollutant concentrations of diluted gases taken off for analysis.

IS 14600 : 1999 E-2.1.3.14 Quick-acting valves (V), to divert a constant jlow of gas samples into the sampling bags or to the outside vent. E-2.1.3.15 Gas-tight, quick-lock coupling elements (e) between the quick-acting valves and the sampling bags shall be used. The coupling shall close automatically on the sampling-bag side; as an alternative, other ways of transporting the samples to the analyser may be used (for example, three-way stopcocks). E-2.1.3.16 Bags (B) shall be for collecting samples of the diluted exhaust gas and of the dilution air during the test. They shall be of sufficient capacity not to impede the sample flow. The bag material shall be such that it does not affect either the measurement or the chemical composition of the gas samples (for example, laminated polyethylene/polyamide films, or fluorinated polyhydrocarbons). E-2.1.3.17 A digital counter (C') shall be used to register the number of revolutions performed by the positive displacement pump during the test. E-2.1.4 Additional equipment if any required shall be used while testing diesel engine vehicles. shall be maintained at sonic velocity R hich is directly proportional to the square root of the gas temperature. Flow is continually monitored, computed, and integrated over the test. If an additional critical-flow sampling venturi is used, the proportionality of the gas samples taken shall be ensured. As both pressure and temperature are equal at the two venturi inlets, the volume of the gas flow diverted for sampling is proportional to the total volume of diluted exhaust gas mixture produced and thus the requirements of this test are met. E-2.2.2 A schematic drawing of such a sampling system is shown in Fig. 11. Since various configurations can produce accurate results, exact conformity with the drawing is not essential. Additional components such as instruments, valves, solenoids and switches may be used to provide additional information and co-ordinate the functions of the component system. E-2.2.3.11 Quick-acting solenoid valves (V) shall be employecl to divert a constant flow of gas samples into the sampling bags or to the vent. E-2.2.3.12 Gas-tight, quick-lock coupling elements (Q) between the quick-acting valves and the sampling bags shall be used. The couplings shall close automatically on the sampling bag side. E-2.2.3.13 Bags (B), for collecting samples of the diluted exhaust gas and the dilution air during the test; they shall be of sufficient capacity not to impede the sample flow. The bag material shall be such as to affect neither the measurements themselves not the chemical composition of the gas samples (for instance, laminated polyethylene/polyamide films, or fluorinated polyhydrocarbons). E-2.2.3.14 The pressure gauge (G) used shall be precise and accurate to within 0.4 kPa. E-2.2.3.15 The temperature sensor (T) used shall be precise and accurate to within 1 K and have a response time of 0.1 s to 62 percent of a temperature change (as measured in silicone oil). E-2.2.3.16 A measuring critical flow venturi tube (MV) shall be used to measure the flow volume of the diluted exhaust gas. E-2.2.3.17 A blower (BL) of sufficient capacity shall be used to handle the total volume of diluted gas. E-2.2.3.18 The capacity of the CFV-CVS system shall be such that under all operating conditions which may possibly occur during a test there shall not be any condensation of water. This can be generally ensured by using a blower whose capacity is: i) Twice as high as the maximum flow of exhaust gas produced by accelerations of the driving cycle; or ii) Sufficient to ensure that the CO2 concentration in the dilute exhaust sample bag is less than 3 percent by volume.
